llm.summary: The skill's behavior mostly matches a diary/journal purpose, but it ships with a packaged config.json pointing at an absolute root path (/root/clawd/memory/diary/) which could cause it to read/write unexpected system or other-agents' memory; review/adjust configuration before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (AI diary, quote backlog, curiosity, decisions) align with the included scripts: generate.py collects session logs and persistent diary files; export scripts produce PDFs/HTML. Required binary (python3) is appropriate and expected.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts explicitly read session logs (memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md), diary persistent files (quotes.md, curiosity.md, decisions.md, relationship.md), and write diary entries and export artifacts. They also instruct the agent to spawn OpenClaw sub-agents via sessions_spawn (no raw HTTP). Reading/writing the agent's memory is necessary for the stated goal, but the scripts will access any paths they are configured to use (see config.json).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only installation) and no network download/install of code; scripts are bundled with the skill. This is the lower-risk pattern — code will run locally using system Python and optional native tools (pandoc/weasyprint).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The package includes a config.json with diary_path set to an absolute path (/root/clawd/memory/diary/). If left in place, the skill will read/write that absolute path (overriding workspace detection). That is disproportionate for a personal diary: it may access files outside the current agent workspace or other agents' memory on shared hosts. No API keys are requested, but the skill reads environment variables OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE or AGENT_WORKSPACE to locate workspace — these can be pointed to arbitrary locations.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (normal). The skill will create and update local files (diary entries, quotes.md, curiosity.md, decisions.md) in its configured diary_path — expected for this functionality, but be aware it persists potentially sensitive session content to disk. Autonomous invocation (disable-model-invocation:false) is standard and not flagged by itself.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says (generate and export agent diary entries), but exercise caution before enabling it in a shared/production agent:

- Inspect and remove or edit the bundled config.json before first run. The included config.json points to /root/clawd/memory/diary/ (an absolute root path). Either delete that file or update diary_path to a safe, relative path inside your agent's workspace (e.g., memory/diary/).
- Run the interactive setup (python3 scripts/setup.py) manually so you explicitly choose storage location, privacy level, and which features to enable. Do not rely on the packaged config.json.
- If you want to be extra safe, run the skill in an isolated agent workspace or container to see which files it creates and reads.
- Note the export tools: pandoc (export.py) and WeasyPrint + python-markdown (export_pdf.py) are required for exports; they may fetch external CSS/resources when generating HTML/PDF. Install these dependencies only if you need export features.
- Be aware the skill reads session logs and memory files (memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md). If those contain sensitive data, review memory_integration settings (it can append diary summaries to daily memory) and disable automatic memory integration if undesired.

If you follow the above (remove/change packaged config.json, run setup, and verify diary_path), the skill's footprint is coherent with its diary purpose. If you cannot control these steps or the host is multi-tenant, treat this as higher risk and avoid installing.
